title: The Litany of Loreto
hook: a long chant of Mary's titles
tomorrow: Tower of ivory, house of gold

segments.voice: Yesterday, the undoer of knots: a painting in Augsburg, and patient hands working a ribbon loose. Your line was she undoes knots. Did you slow your hands down? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-one.

Holy Mother of God. Pray for us. Mother most pure. Pray for us. Seat of wisdom. Pray for us. Morning star. Pray for us. One voice calls, the room answers, and the rhythm rolls on, name after name, like waves on a beach. Some parishes sing it on a Saturday evening; some families say it after the rosary, half asleep on the couch. It's called a litany, and this one takes its name from a small hill town in Italy. Today's word: Loreto.
screen: `ONE VOICE CALLS.` → `THE ROOM ANSWERS.` → `NAME AFTER NAME.`

segments.voice: First, the place. Loreto is a shrine town in Italy. Tradition says it holds the Holy House, the house of Nazareth where Mary lived, and pilgrims have come to pray there. This litany was sung at that shrine, and the Church came to call it by the town's name. Second, the shape. A litany is a prayer of call and response. It opens by turning to God: Lord, have mercy; Christ, have mercy; and to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, with the answer, have mercy on us. Then it turns to Mary, and the answer changes. Now it's pray for us. That small switch holds the whole Catholic understanding of Mary's place: mercy is asked of God; Mary is asked to pray. Third, the names. They come in families. Mother: Mother of Christ, Mother of the Church, Mother most amiable. Virgin: Virgin most prudent, Virgin most faithful. Then pictures, borrowed from scripture and old poetry: Mirror of justice, Seat of wisdom, Mystical rose, Ark of the covenant, Gate of heaven, Morning star. Then help in trouble: Health of the sick, Refuge of sinners, Comforter of the afflicted, Help of Christians. And last, Queen: of angels, of apostles, of martyrs, of peace. Fourth, it keeps growing. Popes have added names over time. Pope Francis added Mother of mercy, Mother of hope, and Solace of migrants. Why so many names? Because one never covers anyone you love. A mother is called all sorts of things in a single day, depending on what you need from her. The litany does the same, out loud, together.
screen: `LORETO: A SHRINE TOWN IN ITALY.` · `HAVE MERCY ON US, THEN PRAY FOR US.` · `MOTHER, VIRGIN, PICTURE, HELP, QUEEN.` · `THE LIST KEEPS GROWING.` · then, large: `PRAY FOR US.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray five titles. Settle, and breathe. If you pray, choose five names from the litany and say each one slowly, answering it yourself: Seat of wisdom, pray for us. Health of the sick, pray for us. Refuge of sinners, pray for us. Comforter of the afflicted, pray for us. Queen of peace, pray for us. Let a face come with each one: someone sick, someone grieving, someone far from home. If you don't pray, simply say the five names and let each one rest for a breath. The bell holds the time.
Loreto. A shrine town in Italy, and the name of the litany sung there: Mary's titles, called and answered, pray for us. Today's word.
Your line: many names. Today, notice how many names one person you love goes by, and what each one says about them. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics pray the Litany of Loreto in churches and at home, sometimes after the rosary or at Marian devotions; a leader calls each title and everyone answers, pray for us.

fork.setup: the leader calls, Mother most pure. what does the room answer?
fork.reveal: to Mary's titles the answer is pray for us. have mercy on us is kept for the opening, addressed to God.

trapdoor: what you thought: a long, repetitive list of names.
what it means: a call-and-response prayer that greets Mary by many titles, each answered pray for us.
what a scholar hears: a litany named for the Holy House shrine at Loreto, whose answers mark the line between asking God for mercy and asking Mary to pray.

notes: No dates given for the litany's approval or additions. Pope Francis added Mater misericordiae, Mater spei and Solacium migrantium (2020); 'Popes have added names over time' also covers e.g. Queen of families (John Paul II). Confirm.
The Holy House tradition at Loreto is given as 'tradition says'. The claim the litany 'was sung at that shrine' and took its name from it; confirm.
Titles are cited in common English renderings without quotation marks; the English text of the litany varies. Confirm wording of each title used.
The 'families' grouping of titles (mother, virgin, pictures, help, queen) is the script's own aid. Tower of ivory and House of gold are deliberately left for tomorrow.
Hook: 'some parishes sing it... some families say it after the rosary' kept as 'some'.
